scope: Complete 33-file base-to-head diff and relevant callers.

reviewer_executed.activities: Read-only source, diff, caller, instruction and saved-log inspection; log SHA-256 calculation.
reviewer_executed.log_integrity: All 19 hashes listed in the manifest match the saved logs.
reviewer_executed.checkout: HEAD matches the requested commit; working tree remains clean.

evidence.assessment: Address validation preserves exact encoded identities, including distinct legacy keys. Future domains and collections remain representable.

Validation and conflict projection share the existing domain decoders. Returned choices are detached. Resolution still selects current journal originals and preserves their uninterpreted fields; stale identities are rejected.

Tests cover all six supported domain/collection combinations, deletion, durable resolution, detached ownership, account separation, legacy keys, opaque anchors and retained future records. Coordinator tests cover unchanged-view notifications and same-identity server-copy repair on preferences and SQLite.

Inspected meaningful repair regression failures: both backends expected one notification and received zero. The subsequent 60-test run passed. Final affected run passed 1437 tests with 3 skips; full run passed 3596 tests with 27 skips.

validation_gaps: External plugin-fixture tests were skipped; live plugin round trips and upgrade behavior were not verified.
The intermediate t5-rplx failure at test/reader/unread_records_test.dart:97 remains unexplained. Later passing runs do not establish its cause or a fix.
The new six-kind contract matrix uses preferences storage. SQLite evidence comes from the coordinator, incremental-store and durability suites rather than a duplicate of that entire matrix.

evidence.requirement: One address representation and one supported-value decoding path
evidence.assessment: Implemented in record_address.dart and record_codec.dart. Journal, store and conflict consumers use the shared address parser; labels no longer decode raw record values.

Inspected RecordSync, labels, choice, alert and Sync-page consumers, unchanged Settings waitingChoices at lib/settings/screen.dart:141, and callbacks at lib/catalog/book_page.dart:231 and lib/playback/screen.dart:316. Audited test, integration_test and tool callers. Remaining raw conflict access belongs to journal-level tests and research.

Existing label and widget tests retain device/time fallbacks, duplicate names, catalog titles, chapter and source-revision checks, whole-book audio tracks, deletion choices and bookmark titles. Shared tolerant anchor parsing preserves unavailable previews without tightening record acceptance.

evidence.requirement: Preserve journal authority and persistence behavior
evidence.assessment: No storage or wire-format redesign. Existing pending-write, causal-ordering, recovery and durable-resolution tests remain present. Typed views introduce no persistence-action encoder.

Builder evidence includes baseline 79, characterization 13, focused 160, final affected and full-suite passes. Final analysis reports no issues; formatting reports 31 files and zero changes. The saved complete-diff whitespace log is empty, with success recorded in the manifest. Excluded playback-command, snapshot, writer and product-feature work is absent.

validation_gaps: Execution provenance is builder-run evidence, not an independent reviewer rerun.
Device/browser acceptance, coverage and mutation testing were explicitly excluded and remain with the parent.
The existing external-fixture skips remain acceptance limits; they are not counted as passing integration tests.

evidence.assessment: Address syntax has one owner. Supported value decoding has one shared path. Consumers receive domain values instead of repeating wire-field interpretation, reducing the number of places a record-format change must update.

The journal remains the authoritative state. ConflictVersion's private detached original serves content equality only and is inaccessible to consumers. This preserves recovery notifications without creating a second writer or reconstructing actions from display data.

The shared anchor-preview parser serves two real consumers while retaining their distinct presentation rules. Existing position, bookmark and history types are reused; no general record framework or speculative extension mechanism was added.

Nonempty conflict projection uses the existing worker path. Typed callbacks preserve controller ownership of actions. Existing narrow subscriptions remain in place, with content equality preventing notifications solely from reallocated views.

validation_gaps: No performance measurement was performed or claimed.
Design conclusions are static assessments, supported by builder-run behavior tests; they are not device-performance evidence.

handoff: Pass for the settled ticket scope. Parent retains integration, acceptance, hardening and ticket closure.
